title: Real-World: Age Validator
story: A sign-up form asks for age. Users type anything — negative numbers, 999 years old, random text. Your job is to parse it, validate it makes sense, and return either a clean number or a helpful explanation.
why: The age validator demonstrates the complete parse-validate-transform pattern with Result — a practical pattern used in every form you'll ever build.
analogy: The age validator is like a DMV clerk — they look at your form, check the number is reasonable, verify your category ('adult,' 'senior'), and hand back a validated result. If you wrote '300' as your age, they hand it back with a note.
try_it: Add a `validate_voting_age(age: Int) -> Result[Int, Str]` stage after validate_age. If age < 18, return Err("Must be 18 to vote"). Otherwise pass through. Chain it into process_age. Test with ages 16, 18, and 42.
tips: Separate concerns: parsing, validating, and categorizing are three distinct jobs
Include the user's input in error messages when possible — it helps debugging
The `?` in process_age chains all three steps — each step must return Result for this to work
common_mistakes: Categorizing before validating — an age of 200 would be categorized as 'Senior' incorrectly
Using `<` instead of `<=` at category boundaries — `age < 13` means 12 is 'Child', 13 is 'Teen'
Forgetting to handle the zero case — 0 is technically non-negative but still invalid as an age
